title: fix: migrate traffic summaries instead of rebuilding them
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #15641. Its production Tinybird preview failed twice: rebuilding `generation_usage_hourly` from ~450M raw events exceeded the on-demand populate instance (~10 min, then the server was lost). Production stayed on the previous deployment.

- Adds `FORWARD_QUERY` to `generation_usage_hourly`, `byop_app_daily` and `user_first_activity_mv`, so the deployment migrates the existing summaries (~1.2M rows) instead of re-reading raw events.
- `generation_usage_hourly` maps `everything_else` to `regular`; legacy is unchanged. New rows get all four groups from the deploy onward. Pre-deploy dashboard history keeps operations and dev inside regular (~0.4% of requests, ~6% of Pollen per week).
- `user_first_activity_mv` keeps first-activity states recorded before the regular-only filter. Only five accounts ever sent non-regular traffic (the agent account plus Elliot's and Thomas's four). None registered on or after the KPI start with a first call within 7 days, so D7 activations are unchanged. The weekly KPI usage pipes read raw events and are exact.
- Production check reports all three as "From live deployment using Forward Query"; staging deployment 170 is live with the change.

gist.headline: Move the summaries, not the mountain
gist.blurb: The traffic summaries take the short path through deployment. Roughly 1.2 million existing summary rows are easier to carry than 450 million raw events are to reread.
gist.summary: Adds Tinybird FORWARD_QUERY to generation_usage_hourly, byop_app_daily, and user_first_activity_mv, migrating roughly 1.2M existing summary rows instead of rebuilding them from roughly 450M raw events.
gist.impact: Observability deployments can carry existing summaries forward; generation_usage_hourly maps the old everything_else group to regular while preserving legacy history.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Tinybird traffic summaries as three small labeled crates moving along a short garden path, while a distant mountain of raw event scrolls remains undisturbed. Polli, wearing a tiny moving-day scarf, helps a friendly CRT monitor robot carry a crate; lime-green code-plants and flowers keep the infrastructure scene warm.
